content: Purell is capable of eliminating 99.9% of the most common pathogens that can cause illness within as little as 15 seconds. Its primary active ingredient is ethyl alcohol, which constitutes 62% of the formulation. The product is applied by thoroughly wetting the hands with it and then briskly rubbing the hands together until they are dry. In 2006, The New York Times reported that Purell was widely used by politicians during election campaigns, as they frequently shake numerous hands and need to maintain good health. However, the product is flammable and has the potential to discolor fabrics. The inactive ingredients in Purell include water, isopropyl alcohol, glycerin, carbomer, fragrance, aminomethyl propanol, propylene glycol, isopropyl myristate, and tocopheryl acetate. The product carries a warning to be kept out of the reach of children. According to a report by the Chicago Tribune, there have been instances where children became intoxicated after ingesting Purell.
